Hi Samantha — great to meet you earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps below.

Recap (short):
- Pilot scope you described: inference on a mix of 7B and 13B models, ~5M tokens/mo initial, ramp to ~50M for POC. Concurrent request pattern: bursts up to 40 rps with steady state ~6–8 rps.
- Key procurement ask: clarity on monthly spend slab and whether Redwood will accept monthly POs for pilot vs committed reserved capacity for production.

Preliminary spend slab (ballpark estimates; final pricing depends on model & token mix):
- Low pilot slab (~5M tokens/mo): $300 – $600 / month (estimated $60–$120 per 1M tokens) — hosted, dynamic routing, standard FP16 execution.
- POC slab (~50M tokens/mo): $2,200 – $3,300 / month (estimated $44–$66 per 1M tokens) — recommended: Redwood Dedicated (pooled reserved GPUs) or hosted with committed discount, medium-batch (batch sizes 8–16), mixed-int8 quantization on selected models.
- Production scale (>200M tokens/mo): $6,000+ / month (estimated <$30 per 1M tokens) with Dedicated + caching & aggressive batching.

Notes on assumptions that materially affect unit rate:
- Tokenization: estimates assume 1.0–1.2 input-output token multiplier (depends on prompt templates).
- Model family: 13B with quantization and batching drives costs down; 70B-class models will be 2–3x higher.
- SLA/throughput: lower latency SLOs and higher concurrency increase costs.

Procurement handling options:
- Pilot: Redwood accepts monthly POs for the pilot stage (no long-term commitment), invoiced monthly.
- POC/Production: we recommend a committed reserved capacity (monthly or annual) to get favorable unit economics; we can also do month-to-month with a step-up committed band.

Attachments: redwood_cost_sheet_v1.xlsx (pricing breakout) — see tab "slabs & assumptions".

Next steps (suggested):
1) We send a short SOW draft and a one-pager with the three slab scenarios (today) — Priya to attach.
2) Karthik to confirm model/quantization options and update the unit economics for the specific model mix you expect.
3) Sync with Marcus (procurement) on PO timing and minimum PO thresholds your finance team requires.

Would you be available for a 30-min follow-up on Monday to confirm token mix and procurement timing?

— Priya

Looping in with a few technical clarifications that will change the numbers significantly if the customer adopts different choices: 

- Model mix: please confirm % traffic to 7B vs 13B. If you skew >70% to 7B models we can push the POC slab toward the lower end of the band.
- Output length assumptions: the unit rates in Priya's sheet assume average output of ~30 tokens per request and a ~20-token input. If you expect long-form outputs (100+ tokens) expect 2–3x the costs per request.
- Quantization: int8 / mixed-int8 reduces memory pressure and token cost ~20–40% depending on model; we can provide a quantized-compatible variant for the POC.
- Caching/prefix reuse: if prompts have large shared prefixes we can cache KV and save ~15–25% of tokens served.

I'll run a short recalculation once you send estimated token counts by endpoint. For procurement: we can accommodate monthly PO for pilot. For any committed discount or reserved capacity, minimums start at a $5k/mo equivalent commitment for a discounted tier — happy to map to their PO bands if Marcus shares the threshold list.

— Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
